facts.claim: HSTU (Meta, 2024) beats baselines by up to 65.8% NDCG and is 5.3x to 15.2x faster (achieved, offline benchmarks).
facts.quote: HSTU outperforms baselines over synthetic and public datasets by up to 65.8% in NDCG, and is 5.3x to 15.2x faster

facts.claim: Meta's 1.5T-parameter HSTU generative recommenders improved online A/B metrics by 12.4% (achieved, production).
facts.quote: HSTU-based Generative Recommenders, with 1.5 trillion parameters, improve metrics in online A/B tests by 12.4%

facts.claim: Generative recommender quality scales as a power-law of training compute, like LLMs.
facts.quote: the model quality of Generative Recommenders empirically scales as a power-law of training compute

facts.claim: Centaur is trained on Psych-101: over 60,000 participants, over 10M choices, 160 experiments.
facts.quote: scale, covering trial-by-trial data from over 60,000 participants performing over 10,000,000 choices in 160 experiments

facts.claim: Centaur predicts held-out participants better than existing cognitive models (achieved, lab tasks only).
facts.quote: Centaur not only captures the behavior of held-out participants better than existing cognitive models, but also generalizes

facts.claim: Park et al.: agents built from 2-hour interviews of 1,052 Americans (not 1,000) matched 83%/82%/86% of people's own 2-week test-retest consistency.
facts.quote: achieved accuracies equal to 83%, 82%, and 86% of participants' own two-week test-retest consistency benchmark

facts.claim: Park et al. sample size is 1,052, built from interviews.
facts.quote: Using data from a diverse national sample of 1,052 Americans, we built agents from (i) two-hour, semi-structured interviews

facts.claim: Twin-2K-500 digital-twin dataset: 2,058 US participants, 500 questions, four waves; authors report only early quality checks.
facts.quote: survey a representative sample of N = 2,058 participants (average 2.42 hours per person) in the US across four waves

facts.claim: life2vec used national registry data on more than six million people.
facts.quote: the most comprehensive registry data in existence, available for an entire nation of more than six million individuals

facts.claim: life2vec claims prediction from early mortality to personality nuances (no accuracy number in abstract).
facts.quote: Our models allow us to predict diverse outcomes ranging from early mortality to personality nuances

facts.claim: Fragile Families Challenge: 160 teams, best predictions of life outcomes only slightly better than a simple benchmark (achieved accuracy low).
facts.quote: the best predictions were not very accurate and were only slightly better than those from a simple benchmark model

facts.claim: Fragile Families: 160 teams built models for six life outcomes.
facts.quote: 160 teams built predictive models for six life outcomes using data from the Fragile Families and Child Wellbeing Study

facts.claim: Song et al. 2010: entropy gives 93% POTENTIAL predictability of mobility (an upper bound, not achieved model accuracy).
facts.quote: By measuring the entropy of each individual's trajectory, we find a 93% potential predictability in user mobility

facts.claim: Song et al.: predictability barely varies between people.
facts.quote: we find a remarkable lack of variability in predictability, which is largely independent of the distance users cover

facts.claim: Youyou et al. 2015: computer judgments from Likes beat Facebook friends' judgments (r=0.56 vs 0.49); personality traits, not next actions.
facts.quote: computer predictions based on a generic digital footprint (Facebook Likes) are more accurate (r = 0.56) than those made by the participants' Facebook friends using a personality questionnaire (r = 0.49)

facts.claim: Soon et al. 2008: brain activity encodes a simple free choice outcome up to 10 s before awareness (lab button-press task, above-chance not certain).
facts.quote: the outcome of a decision can be encoded in brain activity of prefrontal and parietal cortex up to 10 s

facts.claim: Aaronson Oracle (Berkeley web version): you press f and d 'randomly' and it guesses your next key with a live rolling accuracy.
facts.quote: Press the 'f' and 'd' keys randomly. As randomly as you can. I'll try to predict which key you'll press next.
